transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep getting startled really bad. Like if a breaker snaps, or a tool drops, or somebody comes up behind me, I jump like I’m coming out of my skin. My heart pounds after, and it takes me a while to calm down even when everyone else is already over it.
Does this startle response happen in most situations, or are there specific places or times when it's more or less likely to occur?

It happens mostly when something sudden happens around me. Like at work, if a breaker snaps or a tool drops, I jump hard. Or if someone comes up behind me, same thing. It’s not really one exact place—it’s more the sudden noise or surprise. My heart starts hammering, and it takes me way longer than everybody else to settle back down.
Do you feel anxious or on edge even when there aren't any sudden noises or surprises happening around you?

Yeah. Even when it’s quiet, I’m still walking around on edge, but it’s more like... I’m mad all the time, and guilty. Like I failed that kid, and somehow everybody can see it on me. It just sits there with me.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and won't go away?

Yeah. It’ll just pop into my head out of nowhere. I’ll see that flash again, or hear the trainee yelling, even if I’m just loading tools in the truck or doing something normal. It hits me hard, like I’m right back there for a second.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because of these memories or feelings?

Yeah. I’ll make excuses to stay away from certain panels or breakers, or jobs that look too much like that one. I’ll try to get someone else to handle it if I can.

And I don’t like talking about that day either. Once it gets going in my head, I can’t shut it off.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself, or like things aren't real?
I don’t know… not really, I don’t think. I mean, I get worked up and kind of stuck in my head, but I haven’t really felt like I’m watching myself from outside my body or like the room isn’t real.
Do you have nightmares about what happened?

Yeah. Not every single time I sleep, but most nights are bad. I’ll be up half the night listening for any pop or buzzing in the walls, and when I finally do fall asleep, I’ll wake up sweating, like I’m right back on that job again.
Do you try to push away or avoid thinking about what happened on that day?

Yeah, I do. I try not to think about it, and I avoid anything that brings it back up. If a job has certain panels or breakers, I’ll make an excuse or try to get someone else to deal with it.

And talking about that day… I don’t like doing it. Once it starts playing in my head, I can’t shut it off.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from the world around you?

Yeah… I guess I do. It’s more like I feel cut off from things. Like my wife or the kids will be joking around, or something good happens at work, and I know I should feel happy, but I just… don’t. It’s like there’s a wall in me or something, and I can’t get to that feeling.
Do you also avoid certain people because of what happened?

Yeah… not so much certain people, I guess, but I avoid places and situations. Like certain panels, breakers, some job sites. I’ll make an excuse not to go near them, or I’ll try to get someone else to handle it.

And I don’t like talking about that day either. Once it gets going in my head, I can’t shut it off.
Do you often feel guilty about what happened on that day?

Yeah… all the time. I walk around feeling guilty and mad, like I failed that kid somehow. Like I should’ve done something different.

And it feels like everybody can see it on me, even when they don’t say anything.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of guilt and anxiety?
Since the accident… the arc-flash on that retrofit job. So, about a year and a month now. It’s pretty much been there since then.
Have you been experiencing any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since the accident?

My sleep’s been pretty bad. Most nights I’m up half the night, just listening for little pops or buzzing in the walls. And when I do finally sleep, I wake up sweating, like I’m right back on that job.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Yeah. I used to always be doing something — staying late fixing up cars, playing ball, helping the younger techs learn the job. Now I mostly just sit at home and let my phone ring. None of it feels worth starting anymore.
Do you ever feel like you're in a daze or spaced out, like you're not really there?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I mean, I get caught up in my head sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed feeling like I’m not there.
Do you ever feel like you're in a daze or spaced out, to the point where you feel disconnected from what's happening around you?
No… I don’t think so. I get wrapped up in my thoughts sometimes, but I’m still aware of where I am and what’s going on. I haven’t really felt disconnected like that.
